Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Las Vegas NV
450 AM PDT Thu Aug 27 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Dangerous heat expected across the Mojave Desert through Friday. 

* Chances of showers and thunderstorms across the region today 
  through Saturday, with gusty winds and heavy rain being the 
  greatest threat.

&&

.DISCUSSION...Through Early Next Week

Well-above-normal temperatures are expected to remain across the 
area through Friday as high pressure remains centered near the Four 
Corners. Record highs were either broken or tied at Las Vegas, 
Kingman, and Desert Rock on Wednesday, and it looks like another day 
of near-record heat before slight cooling on Friday-though 
temperatures will still remain several degrees above normal. The one 
caveat for temperatures today is the potential of seeing widespread 
mid- and high-level clouds, which could hold temperatures down a few 
degrees. The Extreme Heat Warning will remain in place through 
Friday, but it is possible that we could catch a break if the clouds 
are thick enough. An approaching trough over the weekend will help 
shift the high east, lowering heights across the region. This will 
knock temperatures down closer to normal, with highs potentially 
dropping slightly below normal early next week. 

Monsoonal moisture will remain in place over the next couple of 
days, leading to daily isolated to scattered afternoon and evening 
showers and thunderstorms. Due to the position of the high, some 
tropical moisture will be pulled north, with PWATs increasing this 
afternoon as the 1.00 to 1.25 inch contour pushes northward up the 
Colorado River Valley and into portions of Death Valley NP, while 
the remainder of the area generally sees 0.75-1.00 inches. As we 
have seen over the past few days, marginal instability will remain 
over the eastern half of the forecast area along with portions of 
southern San Bernardino County. An approaching trough will also 
bring stronger upper level winds from 700mb up to 300mb, resulting 
in better shear profiles for convective organization. Higher terrain 
will see the best chances of storms, but any outflow boundaries 
could help to generate new storms elsewhere. Any storm will have the 
capability of producing heavy rain, flooding, strong winds, and 
lightning. Mid-range guidance does show drier air advecting into the 
region Sunday into early next week, likely keeping monsoon activity 
at bay for a few days. 

&&

.AVIATION...For Harry Reid...For the 12Z Forecast 
Package...Southwesterly winds will give way to light and variable 
winds early this morning. Winds will pick up and settle from the 
southeast with 15 to 20 knot gusts later this morning, gradually 
veering around to the south by mid-afternoon. Isolated 
thunderstorms are expected to develop this afternoon with the 
potential of some storms impacting the terminal. Gusty erratic 
winds are the main concern with storms, with lightning, brief 
heavy rain, and CIGs below 10kft also possible. Temperatures 
exceed 100F from 17Z-04Z today.

For the rest of southern Nevada, northwest Arizona and southeast
California...For the 12Z Forecast Package...Typical wind patterns
are expected through late morning with winds generally under 
10KT. South to southeast winds will increase in the early 
afternoon across much of the region with gusts 15-25KT expected. 
Convection will develop in Southern Nevada and Western Arizona, 
with more widespread coverage and higher risk for impacts than the
past few days. Gusty erratic winds, lightning, and CIGs below 
10kft are possible with any storms. Further northwest in Inyo 
County, mainly showers are expected. &&

.CLIMATE...Numerous climate locations have a forecast high
temperature and/or forecast warm low temperature within 3 degrees of 
the daily record.

The table below shows the daily record maximum temperature and the 
year the record was last set. An asterisk (*) denotes which records 
are in jeopardy (within 3 degrees of the forecast).

MAX           THU, AUG 27 FRI, AUG 28 
              Record (Yr) Record(Yr) 

Las Vegas     110(2017)*  110(2019)*
Bishop        103(2019)*  103(2017)
Needles       120(1891)   116(2023)*
Daggett       111(2017)   111(2017)
Kingman       107(2017)*  107(2009)
Desert Rock   107(2017)   107(2017)
Death Valley  124(1924)   120(2011)*

The table below shows the daily record warm minimum temperature and 
the year the record was last set. An asterisk (*) denotes which 
records are in jeopardy (within 3 degrees of the forecast).

WARM MIN      THU, AUG 27 FRI, AUG 28
              Record(Yr)  Record(Yr)

Las Vegas     87(2011)*   86(2019)* 
Bishop        67(1970)    62(1970) 
Needles       93(2011)    94(2017) 
Daggett       81(2011)*   82(2017)* 
Kingman       79(2020)*   75(2019)* 
Desert Rock   78(1995)*   77(2011)* 
Death Valley  95(2011)*  100(2019)* 
&&

.SPOTTER INFORMATION STATEMENT...Spotters are encouraged to report
any significant weather or impacts according to standard operating
procedures.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION/CLIMATE...Gorelow
AVIATION...Stessman

For more forecast information...see us on our webpage:
https://weather.gov/lasvegas or follow us on Facebook and Twitter
